name: Edge location estimation via second-order derivative
definition: A method to determine the location of a step edge in continuous unsampled data by finding the maximum of the derivative of the step response, which corresponds to the point-spread function of the acquisition apparatus. In sampled data, this is generally not accurate because reconstruction filters (linear, quadratic, cubic-spline) produce derivatives that are piece-wise constant, piece-wise linear, or discontinuous, making the zero-crossing of the second-order derivative an unreliable approximation of the edge location.
summary: Edge location estimation via second-order derivative identifies step edges by finding the zero-crossing of the second derivative of the reconstructed signal, distinguishing itself by relying on reconstruction filter continuity rather than sample value midpoints.
